proposal.summary: A proof-of-concept exploits a bounds-checking flaw in Windows 10 (SMB3 compression) by sending an SMB2 compression transform header with a large offset value, causing the decompressor to buffer overflow and crash the kernel; PoC compresses an authentication request with offset 4294967295.
proposal.cwe_quote: This contains a modification of the excellent smbprotocol with added support for SMB 3.1.1 compression/decompression (only LZNT1).... header['offset'] = 4294967295

AV.quote: This script connects to the target host, and compresses the authentication request with a bad offset field set in the transformation header, causing the decompressor to buffer overflow and crash the target.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Obtain affected Windows build details and reproduction logs, then verify crash behavior in a controlled lab; if confirmed, coordinate disclosure with vendor and request a patch or mitigations (disable SMB compression) and draft an advisory with detection/mitigation guidance.

evidence_quotes.claim: SMB transform header structure and offset field
evidence_quotes.quote: This header is a small (16 bytes) structure with a magic value, the uncompressed data size, the compression algorithm used, and an offset value.
With further work, this could be developed into a RCE exploit.
